module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 452

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/452](https://www.erdosproblems.com/452)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos452

open scoped ArithmeticFunction.omega

/-- The greatest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere. -/
noncomputable def largeOmegaIntervalLength (x : ℕ) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact Nat.findGreatest
    (fun len ↦ ∃ start, x ≤ start ∧ start + len ≤ 2 * x + 1 ∧
      ∀ n ∈ Finset.Ico start (start + len),
        Real.log (Real.log (n : ℝ)) < (ω n : ℝ))
    (x + 1)

/-- Determine the largest length of an interval in $[x,2x]$ on which
$\omega(n) > \log\log n$ everywhere. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_452 : largeOmegaIntervalLength = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Erdos452

reformulations.difference: The source asks, for large (real) x, 'What is the size of the largest interval I ⊆ [x,2x] such that ω(n) > log log n for all n ∈ I?', an order-of-growth question. The Lean restricts x to ℕ. It measures |I| as the number of consecutive integers (`Finset.Ico start (start + len)` with `x ≤ start` and `start + len ≤ 2 * x + 1`). It takes the maximum with `Nat.findGreatest ... (x + 1)`. It then asks to determine this extremal function exactly: `largeOmegaIntervalLength = answer(sorry)`, with an answer of type ℕ → ℕ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Proved in a scratch file: `len ≤ largeOmegaIntervalLength x ↔ ∃ start, x ≤ start ∧ start + len ≤ 2x+1 ∧ ∀ n ∈ Ico start (start+len), log log n < ω n`, and the value is `IsGreatest` of the good lengths. The predicate holds at 0, is closed under shrinking, and forces len ≤ x+1, so the findGreatest cap x+1 never cuts anything off. Also proved f(0)=0 and f(1)=1, and checked with #eval that ω counts distinct primes (ω 12 = 2, ω 16 = 1). So the helper is exactly the source's maximal |I| for integer x. (2) For real x with m = ⌊x⌋ ≥ 1, the integers in [x,2x] lie between [m+1,2m] and [m,2m+1], so the real-x quantity is within ±1 of f(m). This does not affect 'the size'. (3) Posing 'what is the size of the largest …' as equality of the exact extremal function with answer(sorry) is the repository convention: Erdős 361 and 450 at this commit use the same pattern, and fix PR #4675 moved 361 to it. The exact function determines its growth rate, and CONTRIBUTING.md puts the meaningfulness of the answer term out of scope. (4) The only Mathlib junk values (Real.log 0 = 0, so log log 0 = log log 1 = 0; ω 0 = 0) occur for n ≤ 1, i.e. only when x ≤ 1. That does not matter for the question.

review.notes: No findings. The source statement (erdosproblems.com/452, LaTeX): "Let ω(n) count the number of distinct prime factors of n. What is the size of the largest interval I⊆[x,2x] such that ω(n)>log log n for all n∈I?" Remarks: the CRT gives |I| ≥ (1+o(1)) log x/(log log x)^2, and "it could be true" that intervals of length (log x)^k exist for every k. The helper `largeOmegaIntervalLength` is exactly the maximum number of consecutive integers in [x,2x] with log log n < ω(n); I proved the characterization and IsGreatest lemmas in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The strict inequality, the natural log and distinct-prime ω all match the source. Status: `research open` matches the site (OPEN, last edited Oct 2025) and the teorth data file (open). Will Sawin's forum comment (Jul 2026) gives only an upper bound x^{O(1/√(log log x))}, so the problem is still open; no status issue. Optional additions, not defects: the source's remarks (the CRT lower bound, the (log x)^k speculation) are not formalized as variants. Primary literature: the site cites only [Er37] (Erdős 1937, J. London Math. Soc.), and the forum comment says "Erdős and Graham say they don't know any upper bound". I could not access either (UCSD and web.archive.org were unreachable), so I relied on the precise erdosproblems.com LaTeX.
